question: Can the lazy orbit-member oracle at a tuned factor-base column count c in {1,2,3} drive the Koblitz index-calculus arm at n in {17,29,31} defensibly below its matched strong-rho reference, i.e. with a paired 95% CI that excludes 1 AND an arm order that holds at every §5a pricing weight {0,0.1,1} GAE and at the calibrated weights {0,w_cal,10*w_cal}?

claims.text: Lazy oracle is cheaper than the eager oracle in counted GAE at fixed columns (improvement over the IC baseline; no rho comparison).

Per curve and column count, fully priced distance of the lazy IC arm to matched strong rho; 'defensibly below' only if CI excludes 1 and order holds across the whole band, otherwise 'parity-unresolved' or 'rho-strong-ahead'.

power.note: No formal power computation. Sizing from the committed c=2 n=31 cell (32 targets x 3 rounds, CI half-width ~0.077): 64 targets x 5 rounds should shrink it to roughly 0.05, so H3(i) is decidable only for true effects of roughly 5-6% or more. Each (curve,c) cell is its own test (see amendment A4).

stopping_rules.rule: Fixed n: 64 public targets x 3 rounds per (curve, arm) cell; no early stopping on outcome.
Void a curve if any H1 identity check fails or if the aa-rho paired ratio CI excludes 1.
Void a curve if the positive control (c=2 eager/lazy direction at n=31) is not detected.

decision_rule.text: H2 holds per (curve,c) iff the eager/lazy CI lower bound > 1 at w=0. H3 'defensibly-below-rho-strong' per (curve,c) iff (i) the lazy/rho-strong CI excludes 1 with upper bound < 1, (ii) lazy<rho-strong holds at every w in {0,0.1,1}, and (iii) at every w in {0,w_cal,10*w_cal}. If the order flips at any weight the verdict is 'parity-unresolved' (§5a); if (i) fails it is 'parity-unresolved' or 'rho-strong-ahead' by the point estimate. Each row reports the gap to matched rho as the distance remaining. Each (curve,c) cell is decided on its own interval and every cell is reported; no family-wise statement is made.
decision_rule.statistic: Ratio of total counted GAE (S·sqrt(r)), paired by target, from ecbench compare (schema v2)
decision_rule.interval: ecbench compare primary ci95: linearised (delta-method) t(K-1) interval over K=64 target workloads; ci95_bootstrap reported beside it

inadmissible: Any exponent or asymptotic claim; the algorithm and exponent are unchanged.
Any statement about ECC2K-130, GF(2^83) or deployed curves.
A general 'index calculus beats rho' statement; a positive H3 is a per-curve, per-host, fully priced distance on cold public Koblitz targets.
Wall-time conclusions; the primary unit is counted GAE.
A leaderboard or benchmarks/ row without the validation gate (replay certificate, validator report, matched rho with the §5a band).
Any family-wise statement over the nine (curve,c) cells, e.g. 'some column count beats strong rho'; cells carry no multiplicity correction (amendment A4).
